segment.source: Not used
DNS is not part of this installation (the DNS module or the dns role is not chosen in the previous step), so there is nothing to set here.
Names outside the zones Tenko serves are sent to upstream resolvers. Tenko has none built in: choose the ones your network should use.
Upstream resolvers

One address per line. Start with the resolvers your network uses now: they are in the DNS settings of your router or of a computer (ipconfig /all on Windows, resolvectl status on Linux, the network settings on macOS). The browser cannot read them for you.
Leave it empty to decide later: until a forwarder exists, names outside the zones are refused. Forwarders can be added on the DNS page at any time.
How Tenko asks them
Plain DNS
UDP and TCP on port 53, as most routers and resolvers answer.
DNS over TLS
Encrypted on port 853. The resolver must offer it; you give the name in its certificate.
DNS over HTTPS
Encrypted on port 443 to the path /dns-query. The resolver must offer it.
These are addresses of {name}, which also answers over DNS over TLS as {tls}.
Use DNS over TLS
TLS name of the resolvers
The name in their certificates, for example dns.quad9.net for Quad9, cloudflare-dns.com for Cloudflare or dns.google for Google Public DNS.
Cache, served transports and the query log
Home preset

The Home preset keeps a cache with the bound of the profile, serves no DNS over TLS or HTTPS to the clients and keeps no query log. These are settings of tenko.toml; the result step shows the section to put there.
Use the Home preset
Keep a cache
Answers from the upstreams are kept for their TTL; this profile keeps at most {entries, number} entries.
Entries at most
Serve DNS over TLS to the clients
Port 853 with the certificate of this node; off unless your clients need it.
Serve DNS over HTTPS to the clients
Port 443 on an address of its own, not the port of the console.
Keep a query log
Which names the clients asked for, with the clients pseudonymised; kept on the node only.
Before clients use this node
The node runs the dns role: roles = "controller,dns" in tenko.toml.
Port 53 (UDP and TCP) is free on the listen addresses: no other resolver such as systemd-resolved, dnsmasq or the Windows DNS Server role holds it.
On Linux the process may bind port 53: the systemd unit grants CAP_NET_BIND_SERVICE, or setcap cap_net_bind_service+ep on the binary.
The firewall lets UDP and TCP 53 in from the networks of the clients.
Ports 853 and 443 are free and open for DNS over TLS and HTTPS, and need the same capability on Linux.
DNS upstreams
None yet: names outside the zones are refused
Fix the upstreams: each is an IP address with an optional port.
Give the TLS name of the resolvers for DNS over TLS or HTTPS.
The cache takes 1 to 10000000 entries.
DNS
The upstreams are the default forwarder of the store now; the forwarders page changes them.
The upstreams were not stored as the default forwarder ({reason}). Add them on the forwarders page, or put the section below in tenko.toml.
No upstream was entered: names outside the zones are refused until a forwarder exists.
Put this section in tenko.toml of the node and restart it: the cache, the served transports and the query log are read at start, and the forwarders apply while no rule of the store covers a name.
